The six d=0 tickets have no triple label, so every edge incident to them arises from a pair label. Thus each core ticket has at most 6-d distinct zero neighbours, and each zero vertex has cross degree zeta=6-deg(G[Z]) in 1..6.

Let M=(complement G)[K], N=(complement G)[Z]. Their vertex degrees are m=7-d+sigma and n=zeta-1. Hence 2e(M)=32+r and 2e(N)=r-6, with r=sum sigma=sum zeta. Classify complementary triangles as all-core, all-zero, two-core/one-zero, and one-core/two-zero. For each complementary core edge xy, the number of complementary common zero neighbours is 6-sigma_x-sigma_y+|N_G(x) intersect N_G(y) intersect Z|; the zero-edge analogue is 14-zeta_u-zeta_v+|N_G(u) intersect N_G(v) intersect K|. Summing gives

T(complement G)=6e(M)+14e(N)-sum sigma*m-sum zeta*n+P,

where P consists of the two internal complementary triangle counts and the two common-neighbour counts, so P>=0. Since 6e(M)+14e(N)=54+10r, Goodman gives

T(G)=240-10r+sum sigma(sigma+7-d)+sum zeta(zeta-1)-P
